title: S.B. 365 — Fostering Access, Innovation, and Responsibility in Artificial Intelligence Act; established.
mechanism: A developer of a base artificial intelligence model shall clearly and conspicuously disclose in its terms of service the model name, developer, incorporation location, latest release date, training-data update date, supported languages and a terms-of-service link (§ 59.1-615). Providing that disclosure is not a defense to liability for harm to a plaintiff. In actions against developers, it is not a defense that the AI system autonomously caused the harm (§ 59.1-617). Creates the FAIR AI Enforcement Fund for state agency enforcement of AI system misuse, bias and workforce disruption (§ 59.1-616).
thresholds: Capability-based, no figure: "a large-scale artificial intelligence system model trained on broad and diverse data" defines base artificial intelligence models.

framework.summary: The bill does not require developers to write, publish or follow a safety, risk-management or security framework.

transparency_report.summary: Base-model developers must disclose in their terms of service the model name, developer, incorporation location, latest release date, training-data update date, languages and a terms-of-service link.
transparency_report.quote: shall clearly and conspicuously disclose, in a manner that is appropriate for the medium of the content

incident_reporting.summary: The bill does not require reporting safety or security incidents to any government body.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no shorter reporting window for imminent risks of death or serious injury.

third_party_audit.summary: The bill does not require any independent audit, evaluation or verification of models.

whistleblower.summary: The bill contains no protections for employees who report AI risks or violations.

registration.summary: The bill does not require registering, licensing or notifying a regulator before developing or deploying a model.

shutdown.summary: The bill does not require any shutdown, kill-switch or containment capability.

compute_threshold.summary: The bill does not define coverage by training compute.

revenue_threshold.summary: The bill does not define coverage by revenue, spending or number of users.

harm_threshold.summary: The bill does not define a catastrophic or covered-harm threshold by deaths, injuries or damages for any developer duty.

penalties.summary: The bill states no penalty, fine or enforcement remedy. It creates a fund for state agency enforcement, with expenditures requested in writing by the Attorney General.

effective_date.quote: the provisions of this act shall become effective on July 1, 2027
